theory.intro: A site plan, survey or map is drawn to a stated scale. Convert each measured length to its real length first, then find the perimeter or area from those real lengths.
facts: At a scale of $1:n$, $\text{real length}=\text{plan length}\times n$.
Area scales by $n^{2}$, not by $n$, so at $1:200$ one square centimetre on the plan is $40\,000$ square centimetres in real life.
The safest method is to convert every length to real life first, then apply the ordinary area formula.
$1\text{ m}^{2}=10\,000\text{ cm}^{2}$, so convert square centimetres to square metres by dividing by $10\,000$.
Floor plans usually give lengths in millimetres, so divide by $1000$ to get metres.
steps: Convert each measured length on the plan to its real length using the scale
Find the perimeter or area from the real lengths
State the answer in the unit the question asks for

workedExamples.question_text: A rectangular garden measures $5$ cm by $3$ cm on a plan drawn to a scale of $1:400$. Find its actual area, in square metres.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Use image : original for each length.
$\begin{aligned}\text{length}&=5\times400\\&=2000\text{ cm}\\&=20\text{ m}\\\text{width}&=3\times400\\&=1200\text{ cm}\\&=12\text{ m}\\A&=20\times12\\&=240\text{ m}^{2}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A rectangular courtyard measures $6$ cm by $4$ cm on a plan drawn to a scale of $1:150$. Find its actual perimeter, in metres.
A floor plan gives measurements in millimetres. A rectangular room measures $5400$ mm by $3200$ mm. Find its floor area, in square metres.
On an aerial photograph, a scale bar $2$ cm long represents $80$ m. A rectangular field measures $4.2$ cm by $2.5$ cm on the photograph. Find its actual area, in square metres.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Convert the scale-bar lengths to the same unit.
$\begin{aligned}80\text{ m}&=8000\text{ cm}\\\text{image : original}&=2:8000\\&=1:4000\\\text{length}&=4.2\times4000\\&=16\,800\text{ cm}\\&=168\text{ m}\\\text{width}&=2.5\times4000\\&=10\,000\text{ cm}\\&=100\text{ m}\\A&=168\times100\\&=16\,800\text{ m}^{2}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: On a floor plan, a scale bar $2$ cm long represents $1$ m. A rectangular kitchen measures $7$ cm by $5$ cm on the plan. Find its actual perimeter, in metres.
workedExamples.solution_text: $\begin{aligned}1\text{ m}&=100\text{ cm}\\\text{image : original}&=2:100\\&=1:50\\\text{length}&=7\times50\\&=350\text{ cm}\\&=3.5\text{ m}\\\text{width}&=5\times50\\&=250\text{ cm}\\&=2.5\text{ m}\\P&=2(3.5+2.5)\\&=12\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A rectangular swimming pool is $48$ m long. On a scale diagram it measures $3$ cm long and $1.25$ cm wide. Find its actual area, in square metres.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Use the known length to find the scale, then convert the width.
$\begin{aligned}48\text{ m}&=4800\text{ cm}\\\text{image : original}&=3:4800\\&=1:1600\\\text{width}&=1.25\times1600\\&=2000\text{ cm}\\&=20\text{ m}\\A&=48\times20\\&=960\text{ m}^{2}\end{aligned}$

foundation.question_text:
A plan of a rectangular courtyard is drawn to a scale of $1:200$.
On the plan the courtyard measures $5$ cm by $3$ cm.
Find the real perimeter of the courtyard, in metres.

A plan of a rectangular bedroom is drawn to a scale of $1:100$.
On the plan the bedroom measures $4.5$ cm by $3$ cm.
Find the real area of the bedroom, in square metres.

A plan of a rectangular bathroom is drawn to a scale of $1:200$.
On the plan the bathroom measures $2$ cm by $1.5$ cm.
Find the real area of the bathroom, in square metres.

A floor plan gives all measurements in millimetres.
A rectangular verandah measures $4800$ mm by $2500$ mm.
Find the area of the verandah, in square metres.

A map is drawn to a scale of $1:10\,000$.
A rectangular cemetery measures $1.5$ cm by $2$ cm on the map.
Find the real area of the cemetery, in square metres.

A floor plan is drawn to a scale of $1:50$.
The rectangular shaded part of a kitchen measures $6$ cm by $4$ cm on the plan.
Find its actual perimeter, in metres.

development.question_text:
On an aerial photograph, a scale bar of length $1.5$ cm represents $60$ m.
A rectangular field measures $3.8$ cm by $2.6$ cm on the photograph.
Find the real area of the field, to the nearest square metre.
development.solution_text:
$1\text{ cm represents }60\div1.5=40\text{ m}$
$\text{length}=3.8\times40=152\text{ m}$
$\text{width}=2.6\times40=104\text{ m}$
$A=152\times104$
$=15\,808\text{ m}^{2}$

development.question_text:
A plan of a rectangular house is drawn to a scale of $1:500$.
On the plan the house measures $3.6$ cm by $2.4$ cm.
Find the real area of the house, in square metres.

On a floor plan, a scale bar of length $1$ cm represents $0.5$ m.
The rectangular shaded part of a kitchen measures $10.8$ cm by $7.2$ cm on the plan.
Find its actual perimeter, in metres.
development.solution_text:
$1\text{ cm represents }0.5\text{ m}$
$\text{length}=10.8\times0.5=5.4\text{ m}$
$\text{width}=7.2\times0.5=3.6\text{ m}$
$P=2(5.4+3.6)$
$=2\times9$
$=18\text{ m}$

development.question_text:
On an aerial photograph, a scale bar of length $2$ cm represents $50$ m. A rectangular paddock on the photograph measures $6$ cm by $4.5$ cm.
Find the real area of the paddock, in square metres.
development.solution_text:
$1\text{ cm represents }50\div2=25\text{ m}$
$\text{length}=6\times25=150\text{ m}$
$\text{width}=4.5\times25=112.5\text{ m}$
$A=150\times112.5$
$=16\,875\text{ m}^{2}$

development.question_text:
A rectangular swimming pool is $45$ m long in real life.
On a scale diagram it measures $3$ cm long and $1.4$ cm wide.
Find the real area of the pool, to the nearest square metre.
development.solution_text:
$45\text{ m}=4500\text{ cm}$
$\text{scale factor}=3:4500=1:1500$
$\text{width}=1.4\times1500=2100\text{ cm}=21\text{ m}$
$A=45\times21$
$=945\text{ m}^{2}$

development.question_text:
A plan of a rectangular double garage is drawn to a scale of $1:150$.
On the plan the garage measures $4.2$ cm by $3.5$ cm.
Find the real area of the garage, to the nearest square metre.
development.solution_text:
$\text{length}=4.2\times150=630\text{ cm}=6.3\text{ m}$
$\text{width}=3.5\times150=525\text{ cm}=5.25\text{ m}$
$A=6.3\times5.25$
$=33.075\text{ m}^{2}$
$\approx33\text{ m}^{2}$

mastery.question_text:
A rectangular swimming pool is $56$ m long in real life.
On a scale diagram it measures $3.5$ cm long and $1.65$ cm wide.
Find the real area of the pool, to the nearest square metre.
mastery.solution_text:
$56\text{ m}=5600\text{ cm}$
$\text{scale factor}=3.5:5600=1:1600$
$\text{width}=1.65\times1600=2640\text{ cm}=26.4\text{ m}$
$A=56\times26.4$
$=1478.4\text{ m}^{2}$
$\approx1478\text{ m}^{2}$

mastery.question_text:
A plan of a rectangular double garage is drawn to a scale of $1:125$.
On the plan the garage measures $5.6$ cm by $4.3$ cm.
Find the real area of the garage, to the nearest square metre.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{length}=5.6\times125=700\text{ cm}=7\text{ m}$
$\text{width}=4.3\times125=537.5\text{ cm}=5.375\text{ m}$
$A=7\times5.375$
$=37.625\text{ m}^{2}$
$\approx38\text{ m}^{2}$

mastery.question_text:
On an aerial photograph, a scale bar of length $1.6$ cm represents $75$ m.
A rectangular field measures $4.8$ cm by $3.2$ cm on the photograph.
Find the real area of the field, to the nearest square metre.
mastery.solution_text:
$1\text{ cm represents }75\div1.6=46.875\text{ m}$
$\text{length}=4.8\times46.875=225\text{ m}$
$\text{width}=3.2\times46.875=150\text{ m}$
$A=225\times150$
$=33\,750\text{ m}^{2}$
